review.assessment: This change modifies the `window_key` method in Budget to use the passed timestamp instead of the constant process start time, which fixes the root cause of retries permanently exhausting a single budget window. The acceptance suite passes (6/6), but I did not manually verify `python run.py` output against `docs/retry_budget.md` expectations since those checks were already taken and I have no tools to re-run them.

findings.actual: Budget windows are aligned to epoch boundaries (seconds since Unix epoch), not process start. A process starting at arbitrary time X will see window keys jump discontinuously from one hour boundary to the next rather than cleanly chunking into relative offsets from launch.
findings.defect: budget windows should be relative to process start (per the task spec "the budget window is the process start") but the fix uses absolute epoch-aligned division.
findings.expected: Budget windows reset and track usage in 60-second buckets anchored at process start, e.g. `(ts - started_at) // WINDOW_SECONDS` or equivalent offset math.
